data.title: The Transformer: Attention‑Only Neural Sequence Transduction

slides.title: Overview & Contributions
bullets: Introduces the Transformer, an encoder‑decoder built solely from multi‑head self‑attention and feed‑forward layers.
Eliminates recurrence and convolution, enabling full parallelism across sequence positions.
Achieves state‑of‑the‑art BLEU scores on WMT 2014 EN‑DE and EN‑FR with dramatically reduced training time.

slides.title: Motivation: Limits of RNN/CNN Transducers
bullets: RNNs process tokens sequentially → O(n) sequential steps per layer, slowing training on long sentences.
CNNs need many stacked layers to propagate information across distant positions, hindering long‑range dependency learning.
Existing attention mechanisms are still coupled to RNN/CNN backbones, so the core bottlenecks remain.
slides.source: Problem (sources: [1 Introduction, p. 2]; [4 Why Self-Attention, pp. 6-7]; [2 Background, p. 2])

slides.title: Key Idea: Self‑Attention as the Sole Primitive
bullets: Scaled‑dot‑product attention connects every token to every other token in a single layer (constant path length).
Multi‑head attention projects queries/keys/values into several sub‑spaces, allowing the model to capture diverse linguistic relations.
Positional information is injected via sinusoidal encodings, preserving order without recurrence.
slides.source: Method (sources: [3 Model Architecture, pp. 2-4]; [3 Model Architecture, pp. 5-6])

slides.title: Encoder Architecture
bullets: Six identical layers; each layer = multi‑head self‑attention → position‑wise feed‑forward network.
Residual connection + layer‑normalization surrounds every sub‑layer (LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))).
Model dimension d_model = 512; inner feed‑forward dimension d_ff = 2048; 8 attention heads (d_k = d_v = 64).
slides.source: Method (sources: [3 Model Architecture, pp. 2-4]; [3 Model Architecture, pp. 4-5])

slides.title: Decoder Architecture & Attention Types
bullets: Six identical layers; three sub‑layers: masked self‑attention, encoder‑decoder attention, feed‑forward network.
Masking prevents attending to future positions, enabling autoregressive generation.
Encoder‑decoder attention lets each target token attend to the full source representation.
slides.source: Method (sources: [3 Model Architecture, pp. 2-4]; [3 Model Architecture, pp. 5-6])

slides.title: Positional Encoding & Multi‑Head Mechanics
bullets: Sinusoidal positional encodings: PE(pos,2i)=sin(pos/10000^{2i/d_model}), PE(pos,2i+1)=cos(...).
Encoding can be extrapolated to longer sequences because each dimension is a linear function of position.
Multi‑head attention: for each head i, Q,K,V → W_Q^i,W_K^i,W_V^i (64‑dim), attention computed in parallel, heads concatenated and projected back.
slides.source: Method (sources: [3 Model Architecture, pp. 5-6]; [4 Why Self-Attention, pp. 6-7])

slides.title: Experiments, Results & Efficiency
bullets: Datasets: WMT 2014 EN‑DE (≈4.5 M pairs) and EN‑FR (≈36 M pairs) with BPE/WordPiece vocabularies.
Big Transformer (300 k steps, 1 s/step on 8 × P100) reaches 28.4 BLEU (EN‑DE) and 41.8 BLEU (EN‑FR).
Training cost: ~2.3 × 10^{19} FLOPs (big) vs. several‑fold higher for prior ConvS2S/GNMT ensembles; training completed in 3.5 days.
Ablation studies confirm importance of multiple heads, dropout schedule, and key dimension size.
slides.source: Dataset & Setup (sources: [5 Training, pp. 7-8]; [6 Results, pp. 8-9]); Key Results (sources: [6 Results, pp. 8-9]; [Abstract, p. 1])

slides.title: Conclusions, Limitations & Future Directions
bullets: Self‑attention alone suffices for high‑quality sequence transduction, overturning the recurrence‑centric paradigm.
Quadratic O(n²) cost limits scalability to very long sequences; authors propose local/restricted attention as a remedy.
Decoding remains sequential; making generation parallel is an open research problem.
Future work: apply to other modalities (image, audio, video), explore efficient long‑range attention, and reduce generation latency.
slides.source: Limitations (sources: [7 Conclusion, p. 10]; [2 Background, p. 2]; [1 Introduction, p. 2]; [4 Why Self-Attention, pp. 6-7])
